title: Trabectedin for advanced soft tissue sarcoma
context_label: Adult advanced soft tissue sarcoma after anthracycline and ifosfamide treatment has failed, or when those medicines are unsuitable
indication_text: Adult advanced soft tissue sarcoma after anthracycline and ifosfamide treatment has failed, or when those medicines are unsuitable
purpose: The aim is to control advanced sarcoma and help symptoms. The strongest trial evidence concerns previously treated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma; the team explains expected benefit for your particular subtype.
schedule_summary: Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours starting on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it. The actual dose, start time and any delay require a new safety review.
administration_text: Central venous access is strongly recommended. Trained staff connect the prescribed 24-hour infusion and confirm its actual disconnection time. Dexamethasone 20 mg is given intravenously 30 minutes beforehand. The full visit includes checks, preparation and line care.
monitoring_summary: Use the test-specific schedule below. Blood tests, organ checks and tumour-response assessments answer different questions.

agents.name: Trabectedin
agents.explanation: Trabectedin binds to the genetic material, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and interferes with how cancer cells use and repair it. This can slow tumour growth; normal blood, liver and muscle cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, marked muscle pain or weakness, dark or reduced urine, jaundice, new swelling, breathlessness or line-site pain urgently.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, constipation, mouth soreness and fatigue
Liver injury, sometimes severe; prescribed steroid premedication and blood checks are essential
Muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis), which can cause kidney failure; muscle-enzyme monitoring is required
Heart muscle injury or heart failure; leakage of fluid from small blood vessels can cause swelling and low blood pressure
Allergic reactions and severe tissue damage if treatment leaks outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Blood, liver, muscle and heart checks

anatomy: Report mouth ulcers, soreness or trouble drinking early. Use the prescribed mouth-care and anti-sickness plan.
Report new breathlessness, ankle swelling, faintness or rapid weight gain urgently. Heart tests continue during treatment.
Blood tests detect liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or new significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt assessment.
Muscle breakdown can damage kidneys. Dark or reduced urine, especially with muscle pain, needs urgent assessment.
Low counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness needs immediate oncology contact.
Report persistent diarrhoea or constipation, severe pain, abdominal swelling or inability to drink.
New marked muscle pain or weakness needs urgent review. Blood tests check for muscle injury even without symptoms.
Report line-site pain, burning or swelling immediately. Keep the pump and line-care plan; do not alter settings yourself.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety testing and tumour-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect infection risk, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. Current product information also specifies weekly testing during the first two cycles, then at least once between doses.

monitoring_test_details.label: Liver tests and albumin
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check eligibility, liver injury and protein levels relevant to treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; liver parameters weekly for the first two cycles, then at least once between doses. Repeat sooner when symptoms or abnormal results require it.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess clearance and detect kidney injury, including injury associated with muscle breakdown.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before cycles; extra tests for reduced urine, dehydration, muscle injury or abnormal results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Creatine phosphokinase: muscle-enzyme test
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect muscle injury before it becomes severe.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline, weekly during the first two cycles and at least once between doses thereafter; urgent testing for marked muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart pumping assessment
monitoring_test_details.timing: Heart ultrasound (echocardiogram) or a multigated acquisition heart scan before treatment and every 2–3 months until stopping, as specified in the source complication section. Additional assessment follows symptoms and clinical risk.

monitoring_test_details.label: Infusion line and pump review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Prevent or detect infection, leakage and incorrect infusion delivery.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Check at connection and disconnection; report pain, swelling, leakage, fever or pump problems immediately.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response, symptoms and function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from safety blood tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Review all medicines and supplements, especially strong liver-enzyme inhibitors or inducers, statins and other liver-toxic medicines. Avoid alcohol. Confirm steroid premedication, blood tests, pump training, line care, disconnection and verified contact numbers. Dexamethasone 20 mg intravenously 30 minutes before each infusion is required for anti-sickness treatment and appears to help reduce liver toxicity. This regimen has moderate nausea/vomiting risk; agree the complete prevention and rescue prescription without duplicate steroids. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, a white-cell growth factor, may be used for low counts under local policy; it is not universally required.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Confirm spill or leak instructions and who to call if the pump alarms, becomes disconnected or appears to finish early. Never change settings or disconnect it yourself.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and obtain written contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue after the last dose. Do not assume all drugs have the same waiting period. Contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.

items.title: General chemotherapy risks
items.text: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. evidence.title: Trabectedin versus dacarbazine in previously treated liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma
evidence.summary: A randomised phase III trial in previously treated liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma found longer progression-free survival with trabectedin than dacarbazine. The final analysis did not demonstrate longer overall survival. This supports a disease-control discussion, not a guarantee that treatment lengthens an individual life.
evidence.intro: A randomised phase III trial in previously treated liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma found longer progression-free survival with trabectedin than dacarbazine. The final analysis did not demonstrate longer overall survival. This supports a disease-control discussion, not a guarantee that treatment lengthens an individual life.
evidence.caveat: The trial population had prior anthracycline and another systemic regimen. It does not establish the same benefit for every soft tissue sarcoma subtype. Survival results from first-line doxorubicin/trabectedin induction followed by maintenance belong to a different treatment strategy.
evidence.interpretation: The trial population had prior anthracycline and another systemic regimen. It does not establish the same benefit for every soft tissue sarcoma subtype. Survival results from first-line doxorubicin/trabectedin induction followed by maintenance belong to a different treatment strategy.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: The aim is to control advanced sarcoma and help symptoms. The strongest trial evidence concerns previously treated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma; the team explains expected benefit for your particular subtype. A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.

Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours starting on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it. The actual dose, start time and any delay require a new safety review.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can I restart after a delay or safety hold?
questions.a: Only after the treating team gives an explicit plan. A normal result does not erase a previous severe reaction or permanent-stop decision.

questions.q: Are safety tests the same as checking benefit?
questions.a: No. Safety tests look for treatment effects on the body. Scans, symptoms and function help the specialist assess tumour control.
